mechanism_narrative: A higher current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated rates increase the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, compressing valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above the 75th percentile of its historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0%, it signals economic weakness that prompts monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is elevated, the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over 60 trading days due to the expectation of prolonged restrictive monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS > 3.5.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by HOUST above 1400 and GDPC1 growth below 2.5% annualized), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to overvaluation and anticipation of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1400 and GDPC1 growth < 2.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals an imminent recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity contracts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 300, it indicates high inflation that delays monetary easing, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days as the Fed maintains restrictive policy.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market regime (UNRATE below 3.5% and PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns due to strong economic growth and delayed monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 in the prior month signals robust consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days as the economy gains momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500.
